Mary - Album 1: Bloodlines

Were Bears Here Tonight

"I make the best of what I've got"

Age: 32
Musical direction: dockyard folk-punk / heavy skate-punk; big floor toms, chain-and-wood percussion, gritty bass, rough-edged Mary vocal delivery, gang harmonies, restrained strings during the family-memory section.

[Intro — dock bell / rope strain / crates hitting wood]

“Greg!”

Yeah?

“Last crate!”

Easy—

Easy—

If you drop that one
you’re swimming after it.

…

There.

Done.

[Verse 1]
West Ridge wakes with gulls and engines
Cargo coming with the tide
Ships from places past the water
Feed the whole damn town inside

Grain and timber
Tools and medicine
Things Central needs by noon

Unload fast
Tie her steady
Next one’s docking way too soon

Greg moves freight from ship to shoreline
Carts it inland when they pay
Built his boat from stripped-down timber
Piece by piece and day by day

She ain’t pretty

Neither is he

But she floats
And that’ll do

Every board was cut by hand

Built her stubborn

Built her true

[Pre-Chorus]
Use what’s there
Fix what breaks

Learn the weight
Know what it takes

Hands get cut
Back gets sore

Tomorrow morning
Do some more

[Chorus]
I make the best
Of what I’ve got

A little ain’t nothing
When you’ve lost a lot

Wood and rope
Muscle and time

If it falls apart

I make it mine

West Ridge weather
Forest nights

Keep your head down
Keep things right

You don’t need much
To get along

Just something built
To hold you strong

[Verse 2 — drums pull back / strings underneath]
Was the youngest of six brothers
Four years old when fire came

Forest burned beside our cottage
By the morning nothing stayed

Five big shadows
Gone before me

Family swallowed by the flame

Too young then to understand it

Old enough to know their names

People told me I could leave there
Start somewhere that hurt less bad

Never understood that thinking

It was still the home we had

So I rebuilt every floorboard
Raised the walls and roof by hand

Same patch sitting near the forest

Same old stubborn piece of land

[Pre-Chorus]
Hammer down
Drive it straight

You can’t bargain much with fate

What is gone
Stays gone

What remains—

You carry on

[Chorus — bigger]
I make the best
Of what I’ve got

A little ain’t nothing
When you’ve lost a lot

Wood and rope
Muscle and time

If it falls apart

I make it mine

West Ridge weather
Forest nights

I’ve seen darker
I’ll be all right

You don’t need much
To call it home

Just somewhere yours

Even alone

[Instrumental — dock chains become percussion / dirty guitar solo]

[Verse 3]
Sun goes down across the harbor
Last delivery finally done

Tie the boat beside the piling
Shoulder aching from the sun

Long walk home along the treeline
Same old path beneath my feet

Smoke from chimneys
Crickets starting

Quiet

Simple

Good enough for me

Then I see the door.

…

Open.

That ain’t right.

[Music drops]

Greg.

Think.

Wind?

No.

Lock was good this morning.

Thieves?

Nothing worth stealing.

…

Bear.

Better be a bear.

[Build — low bass / heartbeat toms]
Table sideways
Chair in pieces

Cupboard hanging off one hinge

Blankets dragged across the floorboards
Pantry scattered wall to wall

Claw marks—

Maybe

Hard to tell

Mud tracked through the kitchen

Something big was in my house

Something very bad at manners

[Chorus]
Were bears here tonight?
Did one kick my damn door in?

Were bears here tonight?
And redecorate for fun?

Every cupboard
Every blanket
Every chair turned upside down

If you wanted dinner, buddy

There were easier ways
To come around

Were bears here tonight?
Sure looks like something tried

Whatever made this mess
Was strong

And apparently
Not house-trained

[Breakdown — almost spoken]

No blood.

Good.

No tracks I recognize.

Less good.

Window’s broken.

Fantastic.

…

I just fixed that.

[Verse 4]
I’ve seen black bears near the timber
Seen them wandering after rain

Never seen one open cabinets
Never seen one search this way

Food is scattered
Not all eaten

Nothing obvious was taken

If it came here just for hunger

Why’s my bedroom torn apart?

…

That’s weird.

[Final Chorus — full stomp / layered gang harmonies]
Were bears here tonight?
Maybe that’s the simple answer

Were bears here tonight?
Forest’s right outside my door

Greg knows animals
Greg knows weather
Greg knows what these woods can do

And there’s nothing in this cottage

That I can’t rebuild
Good as new

Were bears here tonight?
Fine

Tomorrow I’ll repair it right

Board the window
Fix the hinges

Clean the floor

And sleep tonight

[Outro — music thins / forest ambience]

I pick up the broken table

Turn it over

Something underneath

…

A mark?

No.

Probably scratches.

…

Yeah.

Bear.

Had to be.

[Distant branch snap]

…

Hello?

[Silence]

…

Great.

[CUT]

TITLE NOTE — STRUCTURAL / FORESHADOWING:
Surface title function: Greg genuinely asks whether bears were in his cottage that night.
Embedded monster echo: “Were Bears” sounds like “Werebears.” This is deliberate title foreshadowing only. It does NOT by itself establish an in-story werebear reveal, species identity, or supernatural fact.
